source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 1 (Fundamentals of Ecology and Ecosystems).

sections.heading: 1. Ecology and Levels of Organisation
points: **Ecology** = the study of interactions among organisms and between organisms and their environment (term coined by **Ernst Haeckel**).
Levels: **organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere**.
**Habitat** = where an organism lives; **niche** = its functional role/'occupation' in the ecosystem.

sections.heading: 2. Ecosystem — Components
points: **Ecosystem** = a community of organisms + their physical environment interacting as a unit (term coined by **A.G. Tansley**).
**Abiotic** components: sunlight, temperature, water, soil, air, nutrients.
**Biotic** components: **producers (autotrophs)**, **consumers (herbivores/carnivores/omnivores)**, and **decomposers (detritivores)**.
Ecosystems are **natural** (forest, pond) or **artificial** (crop field, aquarium).

sections.heading: 3. Ecosystem Function — Energy Flow
points: **Food chain** — transfer of energy through trophic levels (grazing food chain starts with producers; detritus food chain with dead matter).
**Food web** — interconnected food chains.
**10% Law (Lindeman)** — only ~10% of energy passes to the next trophic level; energy flow is **unidirectional** (from sun → producers → consumers).
**Ecological pyramids** (of number, biomass, energy) — the pyramid of **energy is always upright**.

sections.heading: 4. Productivity
points: **Primary productivity** — rate at which producers capture energy (**Gross** and **Net** primary productivity, GPP/NPP).
**Secondary productivity** — energy stored by consumers.
Oceans have low productivity per area but cover most of Earth; rainforests/estuaries are highly productive.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Ecology term = Ernst Haeckel; Ecosystem term = A.G. Tansley.
Habitat = address; niche = functional role/occupation.
Biotic: producers, consumers, decomposers; abiotic: sunlight, water, soil, etc.
10% Law (Lindeman); energy flow is unidirectional.
Pyramid of energy is always upright; GPP − respiration = NPP.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Ecosystem = Tansley; Ecology = Haeckel** (do not confuse who coined which).
**Habitat = place; niche = functional role** (occupation).
Only ~**10% of energy** passes to the next trophic level (10% law).
The **pyramid of energy is always upright** (energy decreases upward).
